hints: Focus on what alkaline aqueous iodine is really testing for, the yellow precipitate of iodoform.
Remember the positive group is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ in alcohols, so check which alcohol in each pair contains this methyl-carbinol unit.
A pair is distinguished only if one gives the yellow precipitate and the other does not, so look for the pair where both give the same result.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

Great start, let us remember the chemistry first. Alkaline aqueous iodine gives a yellow precipitate of tri-iodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$, with a distinct antiseptic smell.

Test condition:
$$\text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{yellow } \text{CHI}_3 \text{ precipitate if positive}$$

**Know who gives a positive result**

For alcohols, you need the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$. Ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, is oxidised in situ and is positive, and any secondary alcohol of the form $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)R}$ is also positive.

**Check pair 1**

Ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, is positive. Ethane-1,2-diol, $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, has no $\text{CH}_3$ group attached to the $\text{C-OH}$, so it is negative. One yes, one no, so they are distinguished. Pair 1 is correct.

**Check pair 2 and pair 3**

Propan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, so it is clearly positive. Methylpropan-2-ol is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$, a tertiary alcohol with no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit, so it is negative. They are distinguished, so pair 2 is correct.

For pair 3, ethanol is positive and butan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is also positive because it contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$. Both give the same yellow precipitate, so they cannot be distinguished. Pair 3 is incorrect.

**Conclude the combination**

Only 1 and 2 allow distinction. That combination of statements is option B.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three pairs. Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly distinguished, but pair 3 is wrong since both ethanol and butan-2-ol give a positive iodoform test.
options.B: Correct because only 1 and 2 work. In pair 1, ethanol is positive and ethane-1,2-diol is negative. In pair 2, propan-2-ol is positive and methylpropan-2-ol (tert-butanol) is negative. Pair 3 fails as both alcohols are positive.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes pair 3 and omits pair 1. Pair 3 cannot be distinguished (both positive) while pair 1 can be distinguished and should be included.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only pair 1. Pair 1 is indeed distinguishable, but pair 2 is also distinguishable and is missing, so this choice is incomplete.
